reviewed_rules.name: Purpose and interpretation
business_rule_summary: Financial accounting converts approved business events into company financial balances while retaining the event, counterparty, dimensions, and monetary measurements that explain every balance. A replacement must reproduce the posting decisions and observable adjustments described here. The records are business records; the design does not require a particular database engine, execution language, or deployment topology. Numerical acceptance examples state inputs and expected results directly; they are requirements for the replacement and do not claim that a running reference application was tested. Derived examples are arithmetic fixtures for the stated rules.

The system has more than one financial history. The general ledger measures debits and credits by account. The party settlement ledger measures invoice and payment allocation. The inventory ledger measures quantities and valuation movements. Asset schedules measure depreciation events by financial book. An invoice's outstanding amount cannot safely be reconstructed from only the general ledger because a later allocation can update the settlement ledger without retagging the original general ledger rows. These histories must remain reconcilable without erasing their distinct purposes.

reviewed_rules.name: Money, precision, and currencies
business_rule_summary: Every general ledger line supports company currency, account currency, and transaction currency debit and credit values. It additionally calculates reporting-currency values. Preserve all four measurement contexts and their rates. The company value supports the balanced journal; account value supports a foreign-denominated balance; transaction value explains the source commercial document; reporting value supports an additional reporting presentation. They are related but are not interchangeable columns.

For normal invoice conversion, company amount equals the already field-rounded transaction amount multiplied by the transaction-to-company rate, rounded to the corresponding company field precision. Summing individually converted rows can differ from converting the summed transaction total; the difference is posted explicitly to a rounding account. Reporting values use the company-to-reporting rate at transaction date when supplied, otherwise posting date. Missing reporting conversion rejects the entry.

reviewed_rules.name: Posting pipeline and balancing
business_rule_summary: The posting request carries the entire proposed entry set for one business event. Ordinary processing validates the current budget rules, inserts required dimension offsets, validates the accounting period and disabled accounts, allocates cost centers, merges eligible entries, normalizes negative sides, creates party settlement entries for applicable account movements, and persists validated ledger rows. A nonempty result with only one ordinary ledger row is rejected. Period closing deliberately uses different settlement and allocation paths.

Merging preserves account, cost center, party kind and identity, voucher line, settled-against document kind and identity, project, financial book, voucher identity, advance kind and identity, and every configured accounting dimension. A row may prohibit merging. Amounts in all three primary currency contexts are added independently. Zero company debit and credit rows disappear after precision rounding except for the specialized exchange gain or loss journal. A rebuild that combines all rows for one account would destroy invoice allocations and dimensional evidence.

reviewed_rules.name: Validation and posting authority
business_rule_summary: Ordinary lines require company, account, voucher kind, and voucher identity. The account must be a non-group account, active, and owned by the posting company. A cost center must belong to the same company and ordinarily cannot be a group. Profit and loss account entries require a cost center. Required accounting dimensions can differ between profit and loss accounts and balance sheet accounts. Receivable and payable entries require the corresponding party context unless a controlled internal operation explicitly suppresses that requirement. Account currency must match the account definition, and party currency compatibility is separately checked. Opening entries cannot post to profit and loss accounts.

Frozen-through dates, account freezing, closed accounting periods, closed financial periods, and restricted dimension values are distinct gates. A user allowed to read or edit an invoice is not automatically allowed to bypass these gates. The posting engine is an internal service boundary: it may create generated ledger records under elevated internal authority only after the originating transaction's permissions and business validations have succeeded. A rebuild must not expose a public unrestricted ledger insertion command.

reviewed_rules.name: Cost center allocation and balancing dimensions
business_rule_summary: Select the latest submitted cost-center allocation whose effective date is on or before posting date and whose company and main cost center match the line. Each child receives each primary amount multiplied by its percentage divided by 100 and rounded to ledger precision. The rounding account is assigned to the first allocation child instead of being split. Budget validation occurs against the main cost center before distribution. Derived example: expense 100.00 split 60 and 40 percent produces child expenses 60.00 and 40.00; a three-way equal split can require a separate journal rounding adjustment.

An accounting dimension configured for automatic balancing contributes offsets only when the proposed journal contains more than one value for that dimension. If several such dimensions qualify, each receives a share of the reversed company debit or credit divided by the number of qualifying dimensions. Offset rows clear party and settled-against links and use the configured balancing account. The reviewed routine places company-derived amounts into account-currency columns; foreign-currency offset-account behaviour needs a dedicated execution fixture before a rebuild treats such a combination as supported.

reviewed_rules.name: Cancellation and correction
business_rule_summary: Cancellation creates reversing entries by swapping debit and credit in company, account and transaction currencies. It also reverses settlement effects and checks frozen and closed periods. The source locks the original matching ledger rows while collecting the reversal set. Under the history-preserving policy, the originals remain effective history and reversals use an explicitly supplied reversal posting date or the current date. Under the alternative active policy, originals and their reversals are marked cancelled and ordinary balances exclude them. These are active policy alternatives; neither should be confused with obsolete data migration. For a new installation, choosing only the history-preserving policy is a proposed scope choice and must be declared.

The reversal must preserve original company, account, party, dimensions, financial book, source references, and values. Separate advance-account reconciliation can reverse only lines matching a specific reference and voucher-line identity. A cancellation must not recompute its financial amount from today's item price or exchange rate. Reporting-currency recomputation during reversal needs a dedicated fixture because reporting values are populated again by the record validation path.

reviewed_rules.name: Financial invariants and command outcomes
business_rule_summary: Let an effective entry mean an entry included by the selected cancellation policy. For an account and reporting interval, the closing company balance is its opening balance plus the sum of effective debits less effective credits. A positive result is a debit balance; a negative result is a credit balance. Income and liability reports may reverse that display sign without changing the stored entry. Account currency and reporting currency balances are accumulated from their own stored amount pairs rather than reconstructed using a current rate.

For posting precision \(p\), define the smallest unit as \(10^{-p}\), and the imbalance as the rounded sum of individually rounded debit-minus-credit values. Ordinary journals and payments permit an absolute imbalance at most \(5\times10^{-p}\); other ordinary vouchers permit at most 0.50. This allowance determines whether an explicit rounding entry can repair the event. It does not authorize leaving a nonzero repairable imbalance hidden in balances.

reviewed_rules.name: Closing, budgets, and consolidated reporting
business_rule_summary: Current closing processing partitions calculation work but retains a single business interval and completion state. Each slice groups effective entries by account and all dimensions, including cost center, financial book and project. Closing reverses the income and expense net balances and transfers the net result to the designated liability or equity account, which must use company currency. Balance-sheet closing values are retained separately. Completion is recorded only after closing entries are written. A submitted closing document whose processing is still in progress must not be reported as completed.

Closing starts on the day after the last closed interval, or financial-year start. Its end cannot precede its start or exceed the financial-year end. If a prior financial year exists with effective postings and no closing record, the reviewed check blocks the new close. A later closing blocks creating or cancelling an earlier close. When perpetual inventory is enabled and at least one noncancelled stock movement exists on or before the close date, the inventory asset ledger balance must equal inventory value after both are rounded to ledger debit precision; a completed whole-company stock closing for the same date must exist and must not predate later changes to relevant stock history. Companies failing either prerequisite do not enter this stock-closing gate.

reviewed_rules.name: Business model
business_rule_summary: Accounts payable records supplier liabilities arising from purchases, reconciles them with receipts and advances, and controls payment. A purchase request authorizes a need, a purchase order commits a commercial purchase, a receipt establishes received quantities and valuation, and a supplier invoice establishes the payable claim. The supplier invoice can itself update stock, in which case it performs receipt-related stock consequences as well. Its financial interpretation depends on stock policy, item kind, linked receipt, valuation category, service deferral, intercompany treatment and invoice return status.

Persistent records include supplier and supplier group, supplier-account defaults, supplier invoice and invoice lines, receipt associations, supplier bill number and date, currency and rate, tax lines, payment schedule, advance allocations, payment holds, withholding entries, general ledger entries and party settlement entries. Each supplier invoice line preserves product identity, commercial unit and quantity, stock quantity and conversion factor, net amounts in both commercial and company currency, expense or clearing account, warehouse, project, dimensions, deferred-service dates where applicable, and source order and receipt line references.

reviewed_rules.name: Liability composition by purchase type
business_rule_summary: The table describes decisions; individual account names are configurable. In particular, the expense-account field on a stock bill may resolve to a clearing account. It must not be interpreted as necessarily a profit-and-loss expense.

A stock invoice without stock update must clear the receipt's liability at the full billed value. If the receipt already posted standard-cost inventory and purchase price variance, the invoice must not post that purchase price variance again. This explicit current branch prevents both duplicated variance and an uncleared receipt liability. An invoice with stock update compares calculated incoming valuation with the resulting stock-ledger value and directs the difference to the appropriate variance account. For standard-cost products, the purchase price variance account is selected; otherwise expense-account fallbacks apply.

reviewed_rules.name: Quantity and stock-value arithmetic
business_rule_summary: For direct invoice receipt, calculated warehouse value is valuation rate rounded to its storage precision, multiplied by commercial quantity and unit conversion factor, then rounded to the line company-net precision. The inspected valuation-rate storage precision is six places when configured valuation precision is at most six, otherwise nine. Where the stock ledger has a different nonzero value, the stock-ledger value becomes the warehouse amount and the difference is posted. Stock quantity and stock value therefore cannot be derived from package count without the unit conversion factor.

A return that changes stock and is either internal or unlinked uses its actual stock-ledger movement when determining the warehouse amount. The comparison basis includes net amount, allocated item tax and landed cost; a sales incoming rate can replace the net basis. This return-specific branch is not equivalent to blindly negating the latest supplier price. Retain historical source references and original valuation context so the return follows its correct valuation path.

reviewed_rules.name: Taxes, landed costs, and withholding
business_rule_summary: Purchase charges have two independent properties: addition versus deduction, and total-only versus valuation-only versus both valuation and total. Total-only tax affects supplier liability and its selected tax or expense account without increasing stock value. Valuation-only tax changes cost valuation but does not add to the supplier invoice grand total. A charge marked for both contributes to the amount due and to eligible inventory or asset value. Capitalization is restricted to the eligible part of the charge; the share allocated to a nonstock item is excluded from capitalized valuation.

Posting a charge in both categories must avoid retaining the same cost simultaneously as expense and inventory. The composition records the ordinary tax movement and the credit that removes its capitalized portion from the charge account. When the earlier receipt used temporary received-but-unbilled treatment for valuation charges, billing reverses the relevant temporary movement with preserved cost center and project. Rounding residuals in proportional charge cleanup go to the final participating row.

reviewed_rules.name: Payment schedules and advances
business_rule_summary: The shared payment-schedule service can inherit terms from an order only when all lines resolve to the same source order and that order has terms or a schedule. Each percentage installment receives a separately rounded commercial and company amount, and the latest installment establishes bill due date.

A supplier advance is an asset or debit party balance until allocated to a bill. When separate advance accounts are enabled, the original payment retains its own identity and the allocation later transfers the relevant amount to the invoice's payable account. Cancellation of one allocation must not cancel unrelated advance allocations. A bill can be fully settled from several advances and payments, but one reference may not receive an allocation greater than its current available amount.

reviewed_rules.name: Early payment discounts
business_rule_summary: An early payment discount settles the full invoice reference while the bank movement is smaller. The difference can be booked to a discount account alone or split between commercial amount and tax according to configuration. This is distinct from a trade discount applied before invoice tax calculation. In the reviewed numerical expectation, invoice principal 250.00 plus tax 45.00 creates total 295.00. A ten percent eligible early payment discount reduces bank payment to 265.50 while allocated amount remains 295.00. With tax discount splitting enabled, credit deductions are 25.00 to the configured discount account and 4.50 to the tax account. With splitting disabled, the single credit deduction is 29.50. In both cases the payment difference is zero.

These records must retain discount validity date and policy, full reference allocation, reduced money moved, and each deduction. reviewed_rules.name: Invoice uniqueness, holds and release boundaries
business_rule_summary: The supplier's bill number identifies an external commercial document; the internal invoice identity identifies this system's record. When supplier-number uniqueness is enabled and the bill number is nonempty, reject another draft or submitted invoice for the same supplier and bill number whose posting date falls inside the financial-year interval resolved for the new invoice. Exclude the current internal invoice and cancelled invoices. The reviewed search does not filter existing invoices by company: a matching supplier bill in another company inside that interval can block submission. A company-scoped uniqueness rule would be a deliberate compatibility change. A blank supplier bill number does not invoke this duplicate check.

Supplier holds and individual invoice holds are separate authorities. Disabling a supplier hold clears its release date; enabling one without a hold type selects the all-transactions type. For supplier holds, an invoice-only hold affects purchase orders and supplier invoices; a payment-only hold affects supplier payments; an all-transactions hold affects both. The ordinary validation keeps a relevant supplier hold active when no release date exists or today's date is on or before release date. Release occurs after that date, using the current application date rather than the transaction's backdated posting date.

reviewed_rules.name: Business boundary

reviewed_rules.name: Schedules and collection dates

reviewed_rules.name: Credit exposure is not overdue balance
business_rule_summary: Credit limit is resolved from the customer-company setting, then customer-group setting where not bypassed, then company default. Exposure is the sum of effective customer general-ledger debit less credit, the unbilled share of submitted nonclosed sales orders when that component is enabled, and eligible standalone delivery exposure. Order exposure is company grand total multiplied by one minus billed percentage divided by 100. Standalone delivery exposure includes only positive unbilled line remainders without sales-order or direct-sales-invoice links and with a positive company net total. reviewed_rules.name: Claim control and collection reconciliation
business_rule_summary: A claim balance is a signed quantity in a specified currency. An ordinary customer invoice contributes a positive claim; an applied receipt or credit contributes a reduction. A standalone credit keeps its own negative outstanding until refunded or reconciled. Present positive invoice debt and unapplied customer credits separately before presenting a net customer balance. reviewed_rules.name: Declining-balance methods
business_rule_summary: The double-declining annual percentage is 200 divided by useful life in years. Useful life in years is total number of depreciation cycles multiplied by frequency in months, divided by twelve. Round the resulting rate to configured general numeric precision. A five-year life therefore gives 40 percent.

Written-down-value rate can be explicitly supplied. When calculating it, divide residual value by current asset carrying value, raise that ratio to one divided by remaining years, subtract from one, and multiply by 100. Remaining years uses unbooked periods times frequency plus life-extension months, divided by twelve. An explicit rate is preserved during validation; a supplied rate can also remain when residual value is zero. For residual 1000.00, current value 10000.00 and five years remaining, the derived annual percentage before rate rounding is approximately 36.90426555. At two rate places it is 36.90 percent, so residual correction remains necessary.

reviewed_rules.name: Partial periods, disposal, and low-value assets
business_rule_summary: When disposal occurs on or before a planned schedule date, the interval begins after the last scheduled depreciation date or the applicable initial available-for-use date. A prorated charge is calculated through disposal, rounded, and appended at disposal date if positive; generation stops after that. First-period and final-period adjustments depend on month-end anchoring and any useful-life extension. An asset whose rounded first-period charge is not positive can be rejected as too small to depreciate over the selected number of cycles.

Residual correction applies when a final row would leave carrying value different from expected residual, or when any row would push value below residual. Add the difference between candidate remaining value and residual to the candidate depreciation, round, and stop further rows. This preserves cost less accumulated depreciation equal to residual under the intended completed schedule. Do not let a generic rounding routine erase the final remaining cent.

reviewed_rules.name: Depreciation and disposal posting
business_rule_summary: Recognized depreciation debits the configured depreciation-expense account and credits the accumulated-depreciation account for the chosen asset category and company, retaining asset, schedule, financial book, cost center, date and dimensions. A sale or scrap first determines depreciation through disposal date and then removes the asset's financial position. Posting failures must leave the schedule's posting reference and status consistent with whether a journal was actually submitted. The detailed batch-failure and retry behaviour should be verified independently; the existence of a daily scheduler does not establish exactly-once posting.

For disposal, credit the fixed-asset account for net purchase cost and debit accumulated depreciation for its accumulated amount. Profit equals selling amount less carrying value after depreciation; its sign determines gain or loss movement in the disposal account. The sales invoice or scrap journal supplies the remaining counter-entry.

reviewed_rules.name: Value adjustment is a separate accounting event
business_rule_summary: A value-adjustment record retains asset, financial book, effective date, previous carrying value, requested new carrying value, signed difference, difference account, dimensions and generated journal. Reject an adjustment date before acquisition date. The difference is new carrying value less previous carrying value. A positive difference debits the fixed-asset account and credits the chosen difference account; a negative difference credits fixed asset and debits the chosen difference account. The difference account's classification determines whether this represents a permitted expense, gain, reserve or another configured treatment. The generic mechanism alone does not establish statutory permission for an upward revaluation.

After successful journal submission, change the asset's carrying value by the signed difference and update the selected financial book. Regenerate future depreciation while retaining posted schedule rows. The adjustment's previous value is populated when missing; the inspected method does not unconditionally refresh a nonzero caller-provided previous value. reviewed_rules.name: Capitalized repairs and stock consumption
business_rule_summary: Repair cost has two sources: allocated amounts from submitted supplier bills and materials consumed from inventory. A selected supplier-bill expense account must actually occur on the bill for nonstock items. Allocated repair cost cannot exceed the remaining eligible amount for that invoice-and-expense-account pair after prior allocations; the same supplier bill cannot be treated as a new payable merely because its expense is later capitalized. Repair cost equals the sum of invoice allocations; consumed-material cost equals quantity multiplied by valuation rate for each consumption row; total repair cost is their sum.

Submission creates the material issue when consumption rows exist. When capitalization is enabled, increase total asset cost, additional capitalized cost and applicable financial-book carrying values by total repair cost, apply the life extension, regenerate future depreciation and create capitalization entries. For each supplier-bill allocation, debit fixed asset and credit the original eligible expense account. For consumed material, use the material issue's valued amount and expense account for the matching debit to fixed asset and credit to expense. The inventory issue remains the event that credits inventory; the capitalization must not credit inventory again.

reviewed_rules.name: Recognition and claim are independent
business_rule_summary: An invoice establishes a claim or obligation at its document date. Revenue or expense recognition can be spread over the period in which the service is provided. reviewed_rules.name: Interval progression and recovery
business_rule_summary: The next recognition interval starts on the service start date, or one day after the latest applicable recorded recognition date. Discovery considers direct ledger recognition and relevant linked journals, including a draft journal that has reserved the interval. The interval normally ends at month end, capped by service end, stop date where applicable, and processing cutoff. An interval with start later than end produces no booking. When several intervals are due, calculation continues until the cutoff or final interval, but stops on an accounting error.

Recognition can create direct ledger entries or linked journals according to policy. Journal creation and journal submission are separate choices: a generated draft is not recognized financial income. Persist the distinction between calculated, journal-created, posted and failed outcomes. reviewed_rules.name: Daily recognition arithmetic

reviewed_rules.name: Monthly recognition arithmetic
business_rule_summary: The monthly method counts calendar months touched by the interval, then multiplies that count by a prorate factor. The factor is date difference between service end and service start divided by date difference from the first day of the starting month to the last day of the ending month. Unlike the daily method, these differences omit the inclusive extra day. Round the resulting effective month count to one decimal place.

A nonfinal month's base charge is company net amount divided by effective month count, rounded to the company amount precision and capped so cumulative recognized value cannot exceed line value. If the account is foreign currency, perform the analogous calculation in transaction amount. A partial booking month then multiplies the charge by its rounded-to-one-decimal partial-month ratio. The partial ratio uses booking-end less booking-start divided by ending-month last day less starting-month first day. The final interval again uses exact residual.
